title: Sequencer crash-recovery checkpoint is shared by every instance on the machine; a second instance is offered another run's live sequence and cannot dismiss the prompt
what_happened: My sandboxed instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/planning/data; DB had 0 sequences, 0 sequence_runs, 0 sequence_checkpoints, 0 captured_images) put up a modal "Recover Sequence? A previous sequence was interrupted and can be resumed. Sequence: New Sequence, Saved: 2m ago, Completed: 6 frames (0m integration)". The log line was 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' — the shared user support dir, not the configured data dir. That file (skotiq_session.checkpoint, mtime advancing every few seconds, containing a 20x3s "Take Exposures" node I never created) belongs to a different Skotiq process running concurrently. Clicking "Discard" three times did not dismiss the dialog — the other process rewrote the checkpoint within ~3s each time, so the app re-detected it and re-prompted, leaving the GUI wedged behind a modal barrier (barrierDismissible:false, Escape ignored). I had to relaunch with XDG_DATA_HOME redirected to escape it.
expected: The checkpoint must live under the instance's own data root (SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR / the profile's directory), so two Skotiq processes on one machine — the documented desktop-GUI + headless-appliance pairing, or two profiles — never see each other's run. "Resume" here would have loaded and started a sequence belonging to another rig.
repro: 1. Run two Skotiq desktop instances on one machine with different SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR/SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR. 2. Start a sequence in instance A. 3. Launch/relaunch instance B -> "Recover Sequence?" appears in B describing A's run. 4. Click Discard repeatedly while A is still checkpointing -> dialog reappears each time.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-77-plan-nofw.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-81-discarded.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-82-discard2.png, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-83-discard3.png; /tmp/ns-audit/planning/app.log line 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop'; head of /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint
proposed_fix: Resolve the checkpoint directory the same way the DB path is resolved — honour SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR (and the headless code's `<support>/checkpoints` sub-directory convention from apps/desktop/lib/headless/host_checkpoint_directory.dart:14-33) instead of the bare application-support root. Additionally, after a Discard that is immediately followed by a fresh checkpoint from another writer, do not silently re-prompt in a loop: record the discarded checkpoint id/timestamp and suppress it, and give the dialog a "Not now" escape.
verdict_reasoning: Core path bug CONFIRMED: my own sandboxed instance (SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR=SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR=/tmp/ns-audit/planning-verify/data) logged 'Setting checkpoint directory to: /home/scdouglas/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop' (/tmp/ns-audit/planning-verify/app.log), i.e. the shared per-app support root, not the configured data dir. Source confirms: app_shell.dart:342-348 passes the bare getApplicationSupportDirectory() to backend.sequencerSetCheckpointDir. Dialog details confirmed too (app_shell.dart:373 barrierDismissible:false; only 'Discard'/'Resume' actions at :450-464; no 'Not now'). TWO SUPPORTING CLAIMS REFUTED. (1) 'the documented desktop-GUI + headless-appliance pairing' would collide: it would not. The headless host resolves <support>/checkpoints (apps/desktop/lib/headless/host_checkpoint_directory.dart:14-18) while the GUI uses the <support> root, so they write different files; on disk today only .../com.skotiq.desktop/checkpoints/skotiq_session.checkpoint exists. Only two GUI instances collide. (2) 'Discard three times did not dismiss the dialog because the other process rewrote the checkpoint and the app re-prompted': runAppCheckpointRecovery (app_shell.dart:60-83) loops ONLY when resume()/discard() throws; a successful discard returns AppStartupCheckpointOutcome.discarded and exits. Re-prompting therefore requires backend.discardCheckpoint to throw, which the finding does not establish and I could not reproduce. SEVERITY corrected P1 -> P3: production installs are one-instance-per-data-dir (the app takes a per-data-dir single-instance lock), so the blast radius is the audit harness / a deliberately multi-profile user, not a shipping rig.

title: Sunrise and sunset are 3.5-4 minutes wrong (atmospheric refraction counted twice)
what_happened: The dashboard night-timeline strip for 40.0N/-75.0W on 2026-08-01 shows Sunset 20:17 and Sunrise 05:55 (and Astro dark 22:01, Astro dawn 04:11). Ground truth (astropy, 15-second grid, sun centre at the standard -0.833 deg upper-limb altitude): sunset 20:13:30, sunrise 05:59:15, astronomical dusk 22:01:30, astronomical dawn 04:11:15. The two twilight numbers are right to under a minute; only sunrise/sunset are off, and symmetrically outward — the app reports 7.5 minutes more daylight than reality. Reverse-solving, the app's sunset time corresponds to a geometric sun altitude of about -1.4 deg, i.e. -0.833 deg plus another ~34' of refraction.
expected: Sunset 20:13 / sunrise 05:59 (matching USNO/NOAA/astropy to the minute).
repro: Set location 40 / -75 / 100m, open Dashboard, read the 'ASTRO DARK IN' timeline strip labels.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-77-plan-nofw.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-81-discarded.png (Sunset 20:17, Astro dark 22:01, Astro dawn 04:11, Sunrise 05:55); astropy cross-check output in the transcript
where: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:940-955 (_apparentAltitudeOf returns trueToApparentAltitude(trueAlt), i.e. geometric + ~34' refraction) used as the search function at :612 and :668 against `_sunRiseSetAltitude = -0.8333` (:483-484), whose own comment says it is "-34' (refraction) - 16' (semi-diameter)"
proposed_fix: Pick one convention. Either search the GEOMETRIC altitude for -0.8333 deg, or keep searching apparent altitude and change the target to -16' (-0.2667 deg, semi-diameter only). The same double-count applies to `_moonRiseSetAltitude = -0.7` at :486-487, so moonrise/moonset are biased the same way. Twilights are unaffected because the Bennett refraction term is suppressed well below the horizon (:139).
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and independently cross-checked. The dashboard night strip for 40.0N/-75.0W on 2026-08-01 reads Sunset 20:17, Astro dark 22:01, Astro dawn 04:11, Sunrise 05:55 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-26-dash2.png). My own NOAA solar-position solve on a 30 s grid with 40-step bisection (script in scratchpad/sun.py, sun centre at geometric -0.8333 deg) gives sunset 20:13:38, astro dusk 22:01:45, astro dawn 04:11:17, sunrise 05:59:25 - the two twilights agree to under a minute, sunset is 3.4 min late and sunrise 4.4 min early, symmetric and outward exactly as claimed. Mechanism confirmed: the crossing search evaluates APPARENT altitude (sunAltitude has apparent:true by default and returns trueToApparentAltitude(trueAlt), astronomy_calculations.dart:458-473) against a target of -0.8333 deg whose own comment says it already contains -34' of refraction (:483-484), so ~34' is counted twice; twilight angles are unaffected because atmosphericRefraction returns 0 below -2 deg (:508). CITATION CORRECTION: the twilight path uses sunAltitude at lines 615 and 671, not _apparentAltitudeOf at 612/668 - though _apparentAltitudeOf carries the identical double-count on the calculateObjectVisibility sun/moon path (standardAltitude: _sunRiseSetAltitude at :1218 and _moonRiseSetAltitude at :1237), so the moon claim is plausible on the same grounds. SEVERITY corrected P2 -> P3: astro dark/dawn drive every imaging decision and are correct; only two displayed labels are off by ~4 minutes.

title: "Best night" star lands on the worst night of the week when the project has no targets
what_happened: On a fresh profile, Plan Tonight > Schedule > This Week showed Sat 1 with the star icon and the selected-card highlight, reading '0.0 / 6.2h clear', while Wed 5 in the same strip read '5.0 / 6.4h clear' with no star. NightForecast.score returns 0 whenever bestTargets is empty, so with no project targets every night scores 0, and WeekForecast.bestNight's tie-break keeps the first (earliest) night. The strip therefore recommends a fully-clouded night as the best of the week. Once I added targets to the project the star correctly moved to Wed 5.
expected: With no night scoring above zero, highlight nothing (bestNight == null) — or fall back to ranking by clearDarkHours so the strip is still useful. Never star a 0.0-clear-hours night while a 5.0-clear-hours night is on screen.
repro: Fresh profile with a location set and no project targets: Plan Tonight > Schedule > look at the This Week strip.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-38-target-queue.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-104-schedule.png (Sat 1 starred at 0.0/6.2h); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/planning-132-week-recheck.png (star correctly on Wed 5 once targets exist)
proposed_fix: In bestNight, return null when the maximum score is 0. The widget already renders fine with best == null (WeekForecastStrip passes `isBest: best != null && identical(...)`).
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Plan Tonight > Schedule > This Week shows 'Sat 1' carrying the star icon and the selected-card highlight while reading '0.0 / 6.2h clear' and 'No targets up', with 'Wed 5' reading '5.0 / 6.4h clear' and no star (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-37-schedule.png). Source confirms the mechanism: NightForecast.score returns 0.0 whenever bestTargets.isEmpty (night_forecast.dart:132-139), WeekForecast.bestNight keeps the earliest night on a tie because it only advances on strict > (night_forecast.dart:200-214), and WeekForecastStrip stars whatever bestNight returns (week_forecast_strip.dart:119, isBest also drives isSelected at :149). NOTE ON THE CONTROL: after I added the three targets to the active project the star did NOT move to Wed 5 within the observed refresh - all seven nights still read 'No targets up' - so the reporter's control step is not reproduced here; the defect itself is. P3 correct.

title: The minimum-altitude gate is 25 deg in the scheduler and 30 deg in the planner/sequence builder
what_happened: Plan Tonight > Schedule > Scoring weights shows 'Min altitude 25.00°', and the decision panel rejects with 'M31: altitude 24.3° below site minimum 25.0°'. On the same screen, the Recommendation altitude charts draw their threshold line at 30°, the chips read 'hours above minimum altitude' computed at 30°, and the sequence builder errors with '... at min altitude 30°'. A target sitting at 27° is therefore simultaneously eligible for the autopilot and un-sequenceable.
expected: One minimum-altitude value per site, surfaced in one place, used by the scheduler, the outlook scoring and the sequence builder alike.
repro: Plan Tonight > Schedule > expand 'Scoring weights' (read 25.00°); Plan Tonight > Recommendation > click 'Review in Sequencer' on any non-circumpolar target (error names 30°).
where: SchedulerWeights.minAltitudeDegrees (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/scheduler/scheduler_status.dart) vs SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg used at packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_night_service.dart:699-711; note also targets.min_altitude defaults to 30.0 in the DB schema and is not what the reasoning text reports
proposed_fix: Make the scheduler weight the single source of truth and feed it into SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg and into the outlook scoring, or expose a site-level 'minimum altitude' in Settings > Location that all three read. Also decide whether the per-target targets.min_altitude column is live; today it is 30 by default and the reasoning text quotes the global 25.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on both sides in one session. Plan Tonight > Schedule > Scoring weights reads 'Min altitude 25.00 deg' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/pv-39-crop.png) and the decision panel rejects with 'M31: altitude 15.2 deg below site minimum 25.0 deg' / 'M92: altitude -0.2 deg below site minimum 25.0 deg' (pv-65-week2.png), while the sequence builder on the same screen errors with '... at min altitude 30 deg' (pv-67-crop.png) and the Recommendation altitude charts draw their dashed threshold at 30 deg (pv-36-hero.png). Source confirms the two defaults: SchedulerWeights.minAltitudeDegrees = 25.0 (scheduler_status.dart:131) vs SmartNightSettings.minAltitudeDeg = 30.0 (smart_night_models/settings.dart:195, also the 30.0 fallback in fromJson at :319). The targets.min_altitude column does default to 30.0 in the live schema, as claimed, while the reasoning text quotes the global 25. P3 correct.

title: Night Outlook hero card freezes its "Alt" and "Airmass" readouts while the list card for the same object keeps updating
what_happened: The hero card for NGC6015 showed 'Alt: 14.7°  Airmass: 3.88' at 10:00:55 and still showed exactly 14.7°/3.88 at 10:17:29, seventeen minutes later. In between, the candidate-list card for the same object showed 'Alt: 15.1° Airmass: 3.79' at 10:09:24. The labels are present tense, so the hero card is stating a stale altitude as the current one.
expected: Both cards should track the same clock, or the hero card should timestamp its values.
repro: Plan Tonight > Recommendation. Note the hero card's Alt/Airmass. Wait 15 minutes without leaving the tab. Compare with the same object's card in 'Tonight's candidates'.
proposed_fix: Recompute currentAltitude/airmass for the primary card on the same ticker the candidate list uses, or drop the live readout from the hero and keep only the whole-night figures (peak, transit, window hours) that the section header promises.
verdict_reasoning: Underlying defect CONFIRMED, framing corrected. AltitudeChart computes _currentAltitude/_currentAirmass in _calculateData(), which is called only from initState and from didUpdateWidget when raHours/decDegrees change (altitude_chart.dart:61-72) - there is no timer and no clock provider anywhere in the widget, so the chip labelled present-tense 'Alt:' is frozen at whatever the value was when the widget mounted. Observed consistently with that: the NGC6015 hero card read 'Alt: 21.1 deg  Airmass: 2.76' at 11:46 and still read exactly 21.1/2.76 at 11:53 across tab navigation (pv-29-plan.png vs pv-36-hero.png). CORRECTIONS: (1) the candidate-list card does not 'keep updating' either - it uses the identical AltitudeChart; it only recomputes because scrolling recycles it and re-runs initState, which is what produced the reporter's 14.7 vs 15.1 comparison; (2) the 'where' is wrong - the stale readout lives in screens/framing/altitude_chart.dart, not in _primary_target_card.dart / _recommendation_tab.dart:150-159, and the proposed fix 'recompute on the same ticker the candidate list uses' points at a ticker that does not exist. P3 correct.
